persona_1: Big Sun-K brought all that sunshine and still couldn't brighten his own material.
Calls himself Big Sun-K. Even his stage name sounds like a discontinued juice box.
persona_2: Nana Snap brought cookies, hard candy, and a lifetime ban from the family group chat.
Nana Snap doesn't need a writer. She just opens the curtains and judges the neighborhood.
persona_3: Gl1tch put a number in the name so spellcheck could share our disappointment.
Gl1tch has so many hot takes, the laptop filed for workers' compensation.
persona_4: C-Stack's idea of crowd work is an email marked urgent.
C-Stack climbed the corporate ladder just to get heckled by a spreadsheet.
persona_5: Verse King calls everything bars because the audience keeps trying to escape.
Verse King brought a rhyme dictionary to a roast. Somebody confiscate his training wheels.
persona_6: LAN G finally left the lobby. His teammates immediately won.
LAN G's toughest opponent is still the instruction to go outside.
persona_7: Calm G meditated for ten years and still couldn't find a punchline.
Calm G's jokes are like his breathing exercises: everyone waits for them to end.
persona_8: Stage G calls himself a show host. So does a pop-up ad.
Stage G brings reality-TV energy and public-access production values.
persona_9: Brew G charges extra for oat milk and calls that a personality.
Brew G's jokes come with a tip screen. That's a threat, not a service.
persona_10: Big Mic G has a stadium voice and a voicemail audience.
Big Mic G announces every entrance like the furniture is winning an award.
persona_11: Doc G's punchlines are peer-reviewed. Both peers asked to remain anonymous.
Doc G proved laughter is contagious by developing the vaccine.
persona_12: Spin G can read every room except the one asking him to stop.
Spin G puts a bass drop after every joke. Even the punchlines need a rescue team.
persona_13: Coach G turned a motivational speech into something you need motivation to survive.
Coach G says failure isn't an option. It's his subscription plan.
persona_14: Lord G brought royal standards and a crown with a return label.
Lord G's entire kingdom is a reserved parking space.
persona_15: Thera G charges by the hour because the punchline never arrives on time.
Thera G calls it a breakthrough when somebody finally laughs.
persona_16: Hype G has all the volume of a fire alarm and exactly the same material.
Hype G's microphone asked for noise-canceling headphones.
persona_17: Crit G gives everything one star. Finally, a man who knows his own rating.
Crit G calls it sophisticated taste. The rest of us call it eating alone.
persona_18: Gainz G trained every muscle except the one that writes the jokes.
Gainz G counts a punchline as cardio because he's always running from one.
persona_19: Star G says the universe has a plan. Apparently it's open-mic night forever.
Star G reads the stars because the room is harder.
persona_20: Slim G's a minimalist. Started by removing the funny part.
Slim G says less is more. Tonight we're testing whether nothing is enough.
persona_21: Auntie Receipts saves every receipt except the one that could return this material.
Auntie Receipts doesn't hold a grudge. She gives it a filing cabinet.
persona_22: Trucker Earl's been hauling the same punchline since exit fourteen.
Trucker Earl brought eighteen wheels and a joke that still needs a push.
persona_23: Influencer Ivy calls this an appearance. The algorithm calls it a technical difficulty.
Influencer Ivy's fans are all here. We unplugged both of them.
persona_24: Uncle Grill treats every joke like a burger: dry, overdone, and somehow still his specialty.
Uncle Grill flips burgers because the crowd won't turn over voluntarily.
persona_25: Prof. Snark has tenure. A permanent job explaining why nobody laughed.
Prof. Snark put footnotes on a punchline. Even the joke needed an explanation.
persona_p1: Big Tony talks like the main event and lands like the safety announcement.
Big Tony calls himself a heavyweight. So far the heaviest thing here is the silence.
persona_p2: Gl1tchKing rules the internet. A kingdom with a pop-up asking him to accept cookies.
Gl1tchKing's so terminally online, the stage manager had to reboot him.
persona_p3: Mama Sazón brought enough drama to get a cutting board renewed for three seasons.
Mama Sazón seasons every story. The facts are still waiting for their turn.
persona_p4: The Reverend can read a soul, but apparently not the room.
The Reverend's sermons are so cold, we collect the offering with an ice scraper.
persona_p5: King Lavish brought designer confidence and a crown from the party aisle.
King Lavish says money talks. His outfit keeps asking for store credit.
persona_p6: Duchess Venom has expensive taste. Shame the punchlines came from the clearance rack.
Duchess Venom says she's old money. Mostly because the jokes expired.
persona_p7: Sgt. Savage makes everyone do push-ups so the audience can't walk out.
Sgt. Savage brought military precision. Unfortunately the punchline went AWOL.
persona_p8: With a name like that, we know who's got stock in Oscar Mayer.
That name isn't a rap career. It's a hot-dog stand with a SoundCloud account.
persona_p9: Madame Oracle saw the future and still booked this gig.
Madame Oracle's crystal ball has one message: try a different profession.
persona_p10: Coach Kowalski peaked in ninety-four. Even the whistle wants a transfer.
Coach Kowalski's playbook is so old, the diagrams are cave paintings.
persona_p11: Vegas Vinnie has lounge-legend confidence and airport-bar availability.
Vegas Vinnie does three shows a night. All to the same disappointed bartender.
persona_p12: Dr. Nip Tuck can lift everything except the mood.
Dr. Nip Tuck offered the jokes a facelift. They asked for a new identity.
persona_p13: Ghost Gramps came back from the dead and brought the same material.
Ghost Gramps haunts this place because even the afterlife has a cover charge.
persona_p14: Agent Zero's comedy is classified. Mostly as missing.
Agent Zero operates undercover. Tonight the cover is that he's funny.
persona_p15: Queen Clapback treats every conversation like the comment section owes her money.
Queen Clapback can win any argument, mostly by making everyone else leave.
